Same Merkle-proof withdrawal sent twice: the second call must revert (ZeroWithdraw) — the cumulative cap already covers the leaf balance.
Merkle-proof withdrawal with one flipped hex char in the proof: must revert (InvalidMerkleProof).
Forged ML-DSA-87 signature (genuine signature over a different digest) submitted by the sequencer itself. The contract must reject it: InvalidBatchSignature.

An already-settled batch (same stateRoot, tx-data commitment, encrypted-data hash and ML-DSA-87 signature) resubmitted verbatim. submitBatch binds the signature to the NEXT batch id, so the replayed signature cannot verify against the current digest.

A withdrawal with a VALID Merkle proof that belongs to a different account: the caller passes NotAccountOwner (it withdraws as itself) but the computed leaf (caller, victim's balance, victim's nonce) is not in the tree, so the proof check fails.
A withdrawal against a batchId that does not exist, with the caller's own valid leaf data from a real batch: the batch-existence check fails before the proof is even examined.
